offence_severity: Sections 302, 307 and 34 IPC: death of 8 persons and serious injuries to 18 persons
physical_harm: Death of 8 persons and serious injuries to 18 persons
number_of_offences: Multiple offences charged, but only Ghulam Nabi Guide's involvement was upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes, the conspiracy was hatched and planned in detail
motive: To strike terror in Jammu city on the occasion of Republic Day Celebrations
key_evidence_accepted: The confession of Ghulam Nabi Guide recorded under Section 15 of the TADA Act, which clearly admitted his guilt and described his role in the conspiracy and execution of the bomb blasts.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the confessional statement of Ghulam Nabi Guide as credible, noting that it was read over to him, explained, and he was made to understand its contents, with his thumb impression taken after the statement was complete.
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed on 28.09.1995, supplementary charge sheet filed against Ghulam Nabi Guide

appeal_history.supreme_court: Partly allowed the appeal, set aside acquittal of Ghulam Nabi Guide and confirmed acquittal of Wasim Ahmed Malik

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the confessional statements of Mohd. lrfan and Ghulam Nabi Guide were admissible under Section 15 of the TADA Act and that these statements, along with other evidence, proved the involvement of the accused in the conspiracy and execution of the bomb blasts which resulted in the death of eight persons and serious injuries to eighteen others.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the confessional statement of Ghulam Nabi Guide was inadmissible because it was recorded in Hindi, not in the language of the accused, and that the trial court correctly acquitted both respondents as there was no corroboration of Wasim Ahmed Malik's involvement.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a confession recorded under Section 15(1) of the TADA Act is admissible against the maker, co-accused, abettor, or conspirator, provided it is in accordance with statutory requirements and guidelines, and that such confession can form the basis for conviction, though it should be corroborated when used against a co-accused.
precedent_relied_upon: State vs. Nalini & Ors. (1999)5 SCC 253; Kartar Singh vs. State of Punjab (1994) 3 SCC 569
other_sentence_order: The Supreme Court directed the authorities to produce Ghulam Nabi Guide before the Court for the hearing on sentence and to ensure he is taken in custody forthwith. The Court also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to pay Rs.20,000/- to Mr. Dushyant Parashar as remuneration for his assistance.
